children: Expectations that artificial intelligence will fuel a burst in productivity growth could result in boosting economic growth too much, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Tuesday. That kind of growth risks stoking inflation, which has already remained above the Federal Reserve's 2% goal for more than five years.

"In the next six months, if everyone believes there's huge productivity growth coming, that's a danger to the economy overheating," he said at an event sponsored by the Illinois Manufacturers’ Association.
"There is a very real sense that the bigger the AI hype for the future, the bigger the danger of overheating," said Goolsbee, who is not a voting member of the FOMC this year.

The Fed should rethink its usual policy of “looking through” supply shocks, such as the oil price caused by the conflict in the Middle East. When inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% goal for more than five and a half years, ignoring supply shocks in considering monetary policy is "playing with fire," he said.

"There are some supply shocks that you do need to watch out for, and those are the ones that don't go away," Goolsbee added. The Fed has to consider responding to a persistent shock, he explained. (Updated at 2:04 PM ET).
With the persistence of elevated inflation, "people are irritated. They're annoyed by the economy," he said. And that has worked to erode confidence in public trust.
"The Fed is right in the middle of the Venn diagram," Goolsbee said. "When inflation is high, people are going to have a crisis in public trust."
In discussing the local manufacturing environment, he said, "If you look at the middle market now… demand isn't the problem; it's costs. The middle market is stuck in an uncomfortable spot."
Regarding the national economy, "the hiring rate is as low as the trough of a recession, and the layoff rate is as low as the peak," Goolsbee said. "That's a very unusual situation."
When asked about the federal government's massive debt, he said large deficits act as a stimulus and contribute to inflation.
"I was suspicious of forward guidance" even before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh expressed his view against forward guidance. "I don't like speculating about the rate."

title: Too much AI hype risks fueling inflation, Chicago Fed's Goolsbee says
